question:
An 80-year-old man with a history of Alzheimer dementia (Functional Assessment Staging Tool score
of 4), hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and benign prostatic hyperplasia is
hospitalized due to shortness of breath. On admission, he is afebrile, hypoxemic (oxygen saturation of
83% on room air), and has diffuse wheezing with a prolonged expiratory phase on lung examination.
Treatment with supplemental oxygen, ipratropium-albuterol nebulizers, prednisone, and azithromycin is
initiated for a COPD exacerbation. By the third hospital day, his hypoxemia and wheezing have
resolved, and he reports no shortness of breath. However, the nursing staff notes that he has not had a
bowel movement since admission. On examination, he has mild discomfort with deep palpation of the
left lower quadrant, but his abdomen is soft without rebound or guarding. Senna and bisacodyl are
prescribed. The following morning, the patient is reported to have been awake and agitated overnight,
repeatedly attempting to get out of bed. On evaluation, he is oriented only to his name, believes he is in
a hotel, and repeatedly tries to leave, stating he wants to go home. Which of the following is the most
appropriate step to evaluate his agitation? Answer Choices: (A) Contact the patient’s family to obtain
ancillary history about his cognitive baseline (B) Assess for urinary retention with bladder scan (C)
Conduct a therapeutic trial of increasing the patient’s bowel regimen (D) Check serum electrolytes and
complete blood count (E) Order a head CT scan (F) Monitor vital signs and oxygen saturation (G)
Perform a detailed neurological examination (H) Review medication list for anticholinergic burden (I)
Ask the patient to say the months of the year in backward order (J) Perform a Mini-Mental State
Examination (MMSE)
 A. Assess for urinary retention with bladder scan
B. Conduct a therapeutic trial of increasing the patient’s bowel regimen
C. Order a head CT scan
D. Perform a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)
E. Perform a detailed neurological examination

F. Ask the patient to say the months of the year in backward order
G. Contact the patient’s family to obtain ancillary history about his cognitive baseline
H. Review medication list for anticholinergic burden
I. Monitor vital signs and oxygen saturation
J. Check serum electrolytes and complete blood count
